name: rag-quality-v1
description: Controlled RAG evaluation cases covering retrieval, generation, and abstention.

cases.question: What does retrieval-augmented generation do before writing an answer?
cases.reference_answer: It retrieves external evidence before the LLM writes an answer.
reference_evidence: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves external evidence before an LLM writes an answer.

cases.question: Which stages normally make up a RAG request?
cases.reference_answer: Ingestion, retrieval, prompt construction, generation, and evaluation.
reference_evidence: A RAG request normally includes ingestion, retrieval, prompt construction, generation, and evaluation.

cases.question: What is the output of document ingestion?
cases.reference_answer: Normalized documents with stable IDs and metadata.
reference_evidence: Ingestion converts source files into normalized documents with stable IDs and metadata.

cases.question: Why use a content hash during ingestion?
cases.reference_answer: It detects content changes without relying on file modification times.
reference_evidence: A content hash detects changes without depending on file modification times.

cases.question: What is chunking in a RAG pipeline?
cases.reference_answer: It divides normalized documents into retrieval units that fit model limits.
reference_evidence: Chunking divides a normalized document into retrieval units that fit the embedding and prompt limits.

cases.question: What purpose does chunk overlap serve?
cases.reference_answer: It repeats boundary text so edge-split facts can still be retrieved.
reference_evidence: Chunk overlap repeats boundary text so facts split near an edge can remain recoverable.

cases.question: What does an embedding enable a system to compute?
cases.reference_answer: It maps text to a vector so semantic similarity can be computed.
reference_evidence: An embedding maps text to a numeric vector so semantic similarity can be computed.

cases.question: Which fields must be part of an embedding cache key?
cases.reference_answer: The model name, normalized text hash, and preprocessing version.
reference_evidence: Embedding caches must include the model name, normalized text hash, and preprocessing version in the key.

cases.question: How does dense retrieval rank chunks?
cases.reference_answer: By cosine similarity between query and chunk embeddings.
reference_evidence: Dense retrieval ranks chunks by cosine similarity between query and chunk embeddings.

cases.question: What does Recall@K measure in this corpus?
cases.reference_answer: Whether at least one expected document appears among the first K results.
reference_evidence: Recall@K measures whether at least one expected document appears in the first K retrieval results.

cases.question: What does a reranker do?
cases.reference_answer: It reorders a small candidate set with a query-document relevance model.
reference_evidence: A reranker reorders a small candidate set using a query-document relevance model.

cases.question: When can reranking improve precision?
cases.reference_answer: Only when useful evidence is already present in the first-stage candidates.
reference_evidence: Reranking improves precision only when the first-stage retriever already includes useful evidence.

cases.question: What two constraints does a grounded prompt place on an answer?
cases.reference_answer: Use only supplied evidence and cite stable document IDs.
reference_evidence: A grounded prompt tells the model to answer only from supplied evidence and to cite stable document IDs.

cases.question: What does the evidence-first prompt variant ask the model to do first?
cases.reference_answer: List supporting facts before composing the final answer.
reference_evidence: The evidence-first variant asks the model to list supporting facts before composing the final answer.

cases.question: Why report retrieval and generation metrics separately?
cases.reference_answer: Separating them localizes whether retrieval or generation failed.
reference_evidence: Retrieval metrics and generation metrics must be reported separately to localize failures.

cases.question: What behavior does MRR reward?
cases.reference_answer: Putting the first relevant result near the top of the ranking.
reference_evidence: MRR rewards systems that place the first relevant result near the top of the ranking.

cases.question: What does abstention mean in this evaluation?
cases.reference_answer: Explicitly declining when the controlled corpus lacks sufficient evidence.
reference_evidence: Abstention means explicitly declining to answer when the controlled corpus lacks sufficient evidence.

cases.question: How is false-answer rate defined?
cases.reference_answer: The fraction of unanswerable cases receiving a substantive answer.
reference_evidence: False-answer rate is the fraction of unanswerable cases that receive a substantive answer.

cases.question: How is a conservative cost preflight estimate formed?
cases.reference_answer: Multiply bounded token counts by verified prices and a safety multiplier.
reference_evidence: A conservative preflight estimate multiplies bounded token counts by verified prices and a safety multiplier.

cases.question: Which latency summaries should a report include?
cases.reference_answer: Mean, P50, and P95.
reference_evidence: Latency reports should include mean, P50, and P95 rather than only an average.

cases.question: What is a retrieval miss?
cases.reference_answer: Expected evidence is absent from the retrieved context.
reference_evidence: A retrieval miss occurs when expected evidence is absent from the retrieved context.

cases.question: What is a generation failure when evidence is available?
cases.reference_answer: The generated answer is incorrect, unsupported, or malformed despite present evidence.
reference_evidence: A generation failure occurs when evidence is present but the answer is incorrect, unsupported, or malformed.

cases.question: Which identity fields make an evaluation run reproducible?
cases.reference_answer: Commit SHA, dataset hash, prompt hash, configuration, model IDs, and random seed.
reference_evidence: A reproducible run records the commit SHA, dataset hash, prompt hash, configuration, model IDs, and random seed.

cases.question: Why enable SQLite WAL mode for experiment storage?
cases.reference_answer: It lets readers continue while one coordinator serializes writes.
reference_evidence: SQLite WAL mode lets readers continue while a coordinator serializes experiment writes.

cases.question: How does ingestion support the first part of a reproducible RAG pipeline?
cases.reference_answer: RAG begins by retrieving external evidence, while ingestion prepares normalized documents with stable IDs and metadata.
reference_evidence: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves external evidence before an LLM writes an answer.
Ingestion converts source files into normalized documents with stable IDs and metadata.

cases.question: Which two mechanisms help detect changed sources and preserve facts near chunk boundaries?
cases.reference_answer: Content hashes detect changed sources, and chunk overlap repeats boundary text.
reference_evidence: A content hash detects changes without depending on file modification times.
Chunk overlap repeats boundary text so facts split near an edge can remain recoverable.

cases.question: How do chunking and cache identity work together before retrieval?
cases.reference_answer: Chunking creates bounded retrieval units, and cache keys bind their vectors to text, preprocessing, and model identity.
reference_evidence: Chunking divides a normalized document into retrieval units that fit the embedding and prompt limits.
Embedding caches must include the model name, normalized text hash, and preprocessing version in the key.

cases.question: What representation and comparison does dense retrieval use?
cases.reference_answer: Embeddings represent text as vectors, and dense retrieval compares query and chunk vectors with cosine similarity.
reference_evidence: An embedding maps text to a numeric vector so semantic similarity can be computed.
Dense retrieval ranks chunks by cosine similarity between query and chunk embeddings.

cases.question: Why must first-stage retrieval be evaluated before reranking?
cases.reference_answer: Recall@K checks whether expected documents enter the candidate set, and reranking cannot help unless useful evidence is already there.
reference_evidence: Recall@K measures whether at least one expected document appears in the first K retrieval results.
Reranking improves precision only when the first-stage retriever already includes useful evidence.

cases.question: What should happen between candidate retrieval and a grounded final answer?
cases.reference_answer: A reranker can reorder candidates, then a grounded prompt restricts the model to supplied evidence and stable citations.
reference_evidence: A reranker reorders a small candidate set using a query-document relevance model.
A grounded prompt tells the model to answer only from supplied evidence and to cite stable document IDs.

cases.question: How can a prompt experiment be evaluated without confusing retrieval and generation?
cases.reference_answer: Use a defined prompt variant, then report retrieval and generation metrics separately.
reference_evidence: The evidence-first variant asks the model to list supporting facts before composing the final answer.
Retrieval metrics and generation metrics must be reported separately to localize failures.

cases.question: Which evaluation split and metric expose unsupported answers?
cases.reference_answer: Separate retrieval from generation metrics and report false-answer rate on unanswerable cases.
reference_evidence: Retrieval metrics and generation metrics must be reported separately to localize failures.
False-answer rate is the fraction of unanswerable cases that receive a substantive answer.

cases.question: Which safeguards address hallucination risk and spending risk?
cases.reference_answer: Measure false answers on unsupported cases and run a buffered cost preflight using verified prices.
reference_evidence: False-answer rate is the fraction of unanswerable cases that receive a substantive answer.
A conservative preflight estimate multiplies bounded token counts by verified prices and a safety multiplier.

cases.question: How should an experiment connect performance reporting with failure diagnosis?
cases.reference_answer: Report mean, P50, and P95 latency, and distinguish retrieval misses from failures after evidence is present.
reference_evidence: Latency reports should include mean, P50, and P95 rather than only an average.
A retrieval miss occurs when expected evidence is absent from the retrieved context.

cases.question: What records let a team reproduce and classify a failed case?
cases.reference_answer: Preserve whether evidence was retrieved and record commit, dataset, prompt, configuration, models, and seed.
reference_evidence: A generation failure occurs when evidence is present but the answer is incorrect, unsupported, or malformed.
A reproducible run records the commit SHA, dataset hash, prompt hash, configuration, model IDs, and random seed.

cases.question: How do reproducibility metadata and the RAG stage model complement each other?
cases.reference_answer: The stage model identifies where work happens, while hashes, configuration, model IDs, and seed identify the exact run.
reference_evidence: A reproducible run records the commit SHA, dataset hash, prompt hash, configuration, model IDs, and random seed.
A RAG request normally includes ingestion, retrieval, prompt construction, generation, and evaluation.
